reporting-org.narrative: NGO Fondation Damien, Association de Lutte contre la Lèpre - FONDAM

description.narrative: In 2019, 56% of the new leprosy case detected globally and 26% of the G2D among new leprosy cases were contributed by India In 2020, Globally, 26% of the TB cases and 10% of the MDRTB cases were contributed by India. In India, Bihar is one of the most populous States (128 million) with nearly 90% of the population living in rural areas with a literacy rate of 70.4% and ranks lowest in the Human Development Index of the country. India declared elimination of leprosy at the National level in 2005 but it was declared in Bihar in 2013. Each year Bihar State alone is contributing around 18,000 new leprosy cases i.e., 16% of the total cases in the country. Total TB case notification in Bihar is 78 per 100000 population, i.e, around 52% of the estimated (estimated is 149/100000) in 2020 which is the lowest in the country. The aim of the project application in the next phase is to address important challenges (1) To improve accessibility of quality care to persons affected by leprosy and DRTB through reinforcing functioning referral system in Bihar state and that will ensure access to undeserved / vulnerable population, leaving none behind. This can be achieved by building the capacity of health personnel at each level and by community involvement to enhance early diagnosis at PLRC and ensure specialists and PT at the district hospital for managing leprosy cases and its complications. This will enable patients to get the early diagnosis and treatment (2) Improve the livelihood of PAL through SER and availing social benefits from the Government by getting them disability certificates and engage them in IGA through financial support. (3) Improve treatment initiation of confirmed DRTB patients by tracking, counselling, and facilitating treatment initiation at DRTB treatment centres (4) Improve treatment adherence and treatment success rate among DRTB patients through counselling, monitoring and managing ADR, provision of nutritional supplements and SER.

Our target beneficiaries are people of Bihar, DF’s interventions will be covering a population of 91.808.903 for leprosy in 28 districts and 23.474.131 for DRTB in 5 districts. Around 80.000 PAL and around 2.000 Persons affected by DRTB and their family members would benefit either directly or indirectly during the next phase (2022-26). 90 % of the beneficiaries are living in rural areas. All new DRTB and leprosy patients and all new persons affected by leprosy are also among the target groups.

The outcome will be achieved through specific outputs and activities focused on reinforcing functioning referral system in the districts to improve patient management, medical and social rehabilitation of PAL to improve livelihood and Treatment initiation of all confirmed DRTB cases through early retrieval of loss to follow up cases not initiated on treatment and improve treatment success rate through early identification and retrieval of loss to follow up cases those have stopped treatment.

participating-org.narrative: Direction-Générale Coopération au Développement et Aide humanitaire

description.narrative: Result 1 : A functioning referral system is reinforced. The diagnosis and management of leprosy & its complications is a real challenge. At present PLRCs can diagnose and treat most leprosy cases but in some cases with rare presentation of signs and symptoms an expert opinion is needed to manage cases. DF’s proposal is to facilitate and establish a referral system by linking the health facilities at different levels along with strengthening the referral services at district level.

description.narrative: Result 2 : A system for medical and social rehabilitation of persons affected by leprosy with disabilities is established. Disabilities and deformities are the main causes of stigma and discrimination. Most of the persons affected by leprosy with disabilities face difficulties finding jobs, getting married and pursuing education. It is important to reduce stigma and discrimination by correcting the deformities and preventing the worsening of deformities by engaging them in practicing self-care and their socio-economic rehabilitation.

baseline.value: 0 but 789 persons identified of which 500 could benefit from reconstructive surgery (RCS)

target.value: 35 % to 40 % of 500 will have received RCS
At least 60 % of 500 will have received RCS

description.narrative: Result 3 : The treatment of persons confirmed with DRTB is initiated.It is important to start appropriate treatment regimen for all confirmed DRTB cases at the earliest to prevent further damage of the lungs which can lead to death or lost to follow up.

title.narrative: Indicator 3.1 : Treatment initiation of confirmed DRTB (MR, RR, MDR and XDR) cases increases from 85% to 95% by the end of 2026. (Disaggregated by Sex)

description.narrative: Result 4 : Treatment success rate improves among DRTB patients who started the treatmentDF supported districts are achieving higher treatment success rates compared to State average during 2017-21 with DGD support. But the death rate and loss to follow-up rates are high in 5/6 districts. Treatment adherence, follow-up culture, modification of dosage, management of co-morbidities, adverse drug reaction management and proper nutrition are important factors that contribute towards achieving a good treatment success rate. DF’s proposal is to provide counselling to patients and family members, facilitate follow-up consultation, day-to-day counselling through phone for high-risk patients, provide nutritional supplements and socio-economic rehabilitation for the needy.

title.narrative: Indicator 4.2 : All DRTB patients under treatment will be monitored at least once in 15 days during Intensive phase and at least once in three months during Continuation phase
Indicator 4.1 : All confirmed DRTB patients and family members are counseled within 15 days of treatment initiation throughout the period
